question: R2's last clause: for EVERY loop or sequence in backend/app that re-asks an AI model after a failure, what actually CHANGES between attempt N and N+1?
method: AST sweep (ask calls lexically inside for/while) + grep census of every ask_chat/ask_vision/ask_chat_purposed/.complete call site + call-graph tracing of loops that ask via helpers + live model config read from the running bmv-api container (see retry_site_audit_sweep.txt). Verdicts: DIFFERENT-ASK (attempt N+1 provably differs materially), TRANSPORT-EXEMPT (re-ask only on classified transport failure), VERBATIM (quality failure retried with byte-identical messages+model+params), NO-RETRY (single ask). temp>0 alone is never counted as material variation.

live_config_facts.note: planner/plan_validation/plan_expansion two-model chains resolve to DISTINCT models today, so their identical-prompt failovers are different asks in the live config; they have no dedup guard (unlike architect.py:49-59 and fix_agent.py:166), so an equal-model config would silently turn them verbatim.

verbatim_findings_summary: All six VERBATIM rows are one shape: a retry loop that varies its prompt only when the previous retry made progress (returned usable content), and rebuilds a byte-identical prompt from unchanged state when it did not. No loop outside appspec has an equivalent of generation.py:1270-1281's repair_reproduced_parent_errors identical-error-set early stop.
